rationale: Latin *induratio* means "a hardening/making hard," which is an active process rather than a pathological condition or a physical phase-change. This aligns best with hardening.n.03 ("the act of making something harder"), which captures the general, active sense of the Latin anchor. While hardening.n.01 (pathological thickening) is also a meaning of *induratio* in medical Latin, the OE nominal a-hyrdincg (from *hierdan*, "to harden") is more naturally read as the general act of hardening rather than a specifically medical condition.
